THE LOEWENHEIMS.

Yesterday I had a talk with Mr. who knew the Loewenheimis during his internment in Onchan Camp. agreed that Walter Loewenheim is the dominating personality, thus confirming the impressions of all who know them.

told me that Ernst Loewenheim was employed by Russfoto during his residence in Berlin. This organisation is responsible for the distribution of photographs from the Soviet Union to all other countries and is a cover for all sorts of other Russian activities. This is interesting because it is the first confirmation I have received of statement to this effect. I contrived to ascertain that does not know so that there can be no question of an overlap.

At one time Ernst Loewenheim was an intimate friend of Radek, who was imprisoned after one of the Soviet purges. Ernst Loewenheim often boasted in camp of his many trips to Russia, but declared himself to now be anti-communist. While believing this, declares that the political convictions of the Loewenheimis are based on opportunism and self-interest.

told me that in Berlin Loewenheim had been a prominent personality in the Young Communist movement. He was not quite certain of Walter's main occupation at that time, but knew that he kept a secondhand clothing shop, which, however, for some unknown reason he endeavoured to conceal from all his political friends.

Walter Loewenheim declared in the camp that his internment was due to denunciation from two sources (1) A Nazi agent who had worked in the Thames Engineering Co for some time (2) The communists of the Czech Trust Fund. With regard to these two allegations, it is remarkable that (1) Walter did not do this country good service and himself a good turn by laying information against this Nazi agent (2) The Loewenheimis came over here on their own initiative and had nothing to do with the Czech Trust Fund. Furthermore, Loewenheim wrote a book over here, for which Sir Richard Acland wrote a preface. As Miss Allen, who was responsible for putting forward most of the denunciations prompted by the Communists of the C.T.F., is Sir Richard's niece, it appears to me unlikely that she would have been party to this denunciation. But says that Walter Loewenheim always has a different story to suit the occasion and the listener.
